title: The free-particle relation behind the Schrödinger equation
caption: Substituting ψ = e^{i(kx − ωt)} into iħ∂ψ/∂t = −(ħ²/2m)∂²ψ/∂x² works only if ħω = ħ²k²/2m, that is E = p²/2m. For an electron this is a parabola, E = 3.81 k² eV with k in Å⁻¹: k = 1 Å⁻¹ (λ = 2π Å) has 3.81 eV, and doubling k quadruples E.
alt: Graph of electron energy in electronvolts against wavenumber from 0 to 3 inverse angstroms: a parabola through 3.81 at 1 and 15.24 at 2.
description: The horizontal axis is the wavenumber k in Å⁻¹; the vertical axis is the energy E = ħω in eV.
The Schrödinger equation is satisfied by e^{i(kx − ωt)} only when ħω = ħ²k²/2m: the plane wave carries the classical kinetic energy p²/2m with p = ħk.
For an electron E = 3.81k² eV: 3.81 eV at k = 1 Å⁻¹ and 15.24 eV at k = 2 Å⁻¹.

checks.name: E = ħ²k²/2m = 3.81 eV at k = 1 Å⁻¹ for an electron
